start: Read project:status and project:context; inspect existing changes before editing.
Choose one observable slice; state the outcome, relevant hypotheses, failure risks, verification and recovery before activating it.

Start with the smallest test or runnable example that answers the current uncertainty. Use project:doctor for environment faults, project:impact for the affected scope and check:fast when broader early feedback is useful.

Inspect project/dependencies.json maintenance.next_review_by and advisory expiry when starting active development. If due, add a bounded maintenance task; fresh known-advisory checks run at every integration. No unattended background repair or automatic merge is implied.
during: Validate the most consequential unknown first with a fixture, experiment or failing regression.

Make the first working product interaction available for inspection as soon as it runs. Record the revision and time of an observed demonstration and continue independent work during hosted verification. Owner feedback and engineering verification have separate records.
When new evidence contradicts a plan, record feedback and adjust unfinished work or add a successor task.
Repeat checks after relevant changes, failures or new evidence; avoid retries without a changed hypothesis.
finish: Cover the affected behavior and every required task check on the final execution inputs. Use check:changed, check --task <id> or matching hosted evidence according to coverage. Run an overlapping profile when it adds coverage or helps diagnose a failure. Archive accepted task evidence before completion.

Match verification depth to the failure consequences. Financial calculations need independently expected values, authorization and native isolation need boundary and failure cases, and persistent changes need migration and recovery. Verify protocol compatibility and changes to the verification machinery through their existing protected checks.
Review changed files and accepted history; retain a concrete next action and current focus.
Report tested behavior, unresolved blockers and the difference between mock, native-runtime and release evidence.
Run release-cadence checks at the actual release boundary or through an affected task; normal changes retain a short deterministic feedback loop.

After a coherent delivery is completed and its evidence is archived, assess its PR with project:integration --pr <number> and include the concrete integration recommendation at handoff. Do not wait for future product milestones or for the owner to remember to ask about integration.
Review responsibility cohesion, public boundaries, data ownership and transition cleanup using project/development.json; distinguish engineering evidence from actual owner product feedback.

Archive native Ubuntu Tauri and physical Windows WebView2 observation checks at their designated revisions. Their task-only observations remain historically scoped. Unconfigured or unauthorized external text, voice and client qualifications stay pending until separately observed.
adaptation: Ordinary implementation, local experiments, tests and refactoring within accepted boundaries need no additional owner approval.
Keep investment judgments, runtime permissions and engineering correctness separate.
The development AI records consequential technical changes in ADRs; consult the owner on product experience, data, permission, cost or publication consequences according to project/development.json.

Within the active Herdr session described in project/development.json#/collaboration, assign scoped parallel work when useful, verify the resulting code at one coordinated revision and continue authorized work. Ask the owner for a specific missing input, product decision, acceptance or reserved authorization when needed.
Use skills only for demonstrated repeatable procedures; keep repository facts in canonical records and executable commands.
Split future milestone tasks into observable slices when work approaches; remove speculative work through explicit cancellation and preserve history.

triggers: Repository checks, task lifecycle, CI or local build environment
Wire messages, generated types or operation schema semantics
Synthetic fixture generation, bar aggregation and dataset semantics before runtime integration
Live market subscriptions, provider adaptation, recovery or runtime quality transitions
Interactive chart behavior, visible states or accessibility
Operation authorization, confirmation, revision or idempotency
Persisted formats, migrations, restoration or cache ownership
Computation, preview lifecycle or trusted Python execution
Model, prompt, context, tool policy or collaboration behavior
Installer, bundled workers, startup or target-platform build
Dependency integration, upgrade, removal or license obligations
Local file inspection and chart-data reconstruction diagnostics before provider or runtime integration
Opt-in read-only historical chart integration before live subscriptions, recovery and persistent workspace operations
One bounded rendered market stream, including a late update and the final closed bar.
Visible deterministic market quality and connection transitions.
Profile-bound human model setup, conversation-only projection and text adapter transport

scenarios.user_goal: Inspect a known instrument and understand the source, age and quality of the displayed bars.
scenarios.given: Offline mode, committed synthetic fixtures, one workspace and no credentials.
scenarios.when: Search for each specified instrument, switch timeframes and chart style, and receive bar updates.
then: Selected instrument and timeframe match displayed data.
Synthetic source and connection state remain visible.
The final update is rendered without duplicate subscriptions.

Bridge the history-to-stream boundary from the last included epoch and contiguous sequence. A missing closed bar becomes visible after bounded backfill, or stays visibly gapped. A closed-session history retains separate as-of, coverage, freshness and connection states.
failure_cases: An event arrives during snapshot creation or backfill
Sequence restarts in a new epoch while old events are still arriving
scenarios.evidence_boundary: Synthetic data correctness and chart integration; no real-provider coverage claim.

scenarios.user_goal: Make an authorized change, undo it and recover accepted work after restarting.
scenarios.given: A persisted workspace with a known revision and operation history.
scenarios.when: Apply a human or AI operation, retry it, undo supported changes, then restart or upgrade.
then: Both actors use the same registry.
Accepted state restores without replaying AI actions.
Migration failure leaves a documented recovery route and retained user data.

Execute a confirmed write, lose its reply, reconnect and submit the same idempotency key twice concurrently. Obtain one operation ID and one durable change. Undo that operation with a new receipt; a later conflicting change stays intact.
Restore layout and accepted artifacts with the recorded source disconnected and revoked separately. Keep its identity and visible reason without substituting a sample or issuing a forbidden read.

Explicitly save a typed exchange, memory and strategy in the local profile. Reopen and inspect the same ordered turns, correct a record, delete it and apply an older local backup. A different profile cannot import the backup, and known tombstones suppress old copies.
failure_cases: Changed parameters on a reused key
A different principal tries to replay or undo the operation
Original confirmation arrives after the task was cancelled
Restore interrupted while applying deletion markers
An explicitly opened synthetic sample changes the private timeframe or its eligible undo
scenarios.evidence_boundary: Versioned local state and recovery; no order execution or account integration.

scenarios.user_goal: Experiment with an indicator while retaining accepted results.
scenarios.given: A fixed dataset and an accepted indicator version.
scenarios.when: Create, preview, revise, accept and remove a draft.
then: The same inputs produce the same declarative result.
Preview and accepted layers are distinguishable.
Provenance identifies dataset, engine, code and parameters.

On consecutive expected bars with closes 1, 3 and 5, a two-bucket mean yields null, 2 and 4; population standard deviation yields null, 1 and 1. A three-period override gives null, null and 3. A missing expected bucket yields null in affected windows. Compare a declared parameter, a literal, a null volume and a boolean marker independently.

Interleave two jobs on distinct snapshots, cancel one, accept the visible successful preview once and restart. A later bar close or correction leaves its accepted numeric output and input locator intact.

Run a reviewed trusted Python example with no external inputs on fixed synthetic closes 10 and 14. The mean of the two is 12; the first output is null. Verify all values independently. Preview or rerun under a new input requires fresh human approval. Restart or clearing disposable cache restores the accepted result or identifies its unavailability.
failure_cases: Python attempted with display-only or unknown use rights
Different parameters or warm-up window reuse a prior approval
An expired or cancelled preview completes late
A byte or aggregate point budget is exceeded after multiple output chunks
scenarios.evidence_boundary: Calculation and failure isolation; no financial-performance claim.

scenarios.user_goal: Investigate a chart with AI, inspect its evidence and revise the result together.
scenarios.given: Known workspace context, a versioned mock provider and an explicit research question.
scenarios.when: Select a chart range and discuss an abnormal-volatility indicator. Inspect a source in another panel, correct the selection, then preview, revise, accept or cancel the indicator.
then: Claims distinguish observations, calculations and inferences.
A user who activated the disclosed model connection can finish two ordinary turns with relevant granted fields and tool results without an additional consent prompt.
Execution claims reference actual successful core results.
Context, tool, prompt, model and dataset identities support replay.
The AI reveals the exact row, range or passage for a claim and the user can point back to a different target. Both can return to the previous view.
The affected chart or table shows the proposed change, any required confirmation and the actual outcome.

Issue two tool calls under one task, complete them in reverse order, deny one other call and cancel a waiting task. Verify every reported action against its own correlated core outcome. A worker cannot self-approve a challenge or invoke an internal result-delivery command.
failure_cases: Source revision changed or a passage cannot be located
A reply arrives after the user selected a different target
A duplicate private delivery or a late result after cancellation
The human response arrives after the confirmation expired
An already committed write is followed by task cancellation
scenarios.evidence_boundary: Deterministic mock evaluation; a configured real model needs separate versioned evaluation and owner usability feedback.

scenarios.user_goal: Install, use, upgrade and recover the workbench on the supported Windows target.
scenarios.given: A clean Windows x64 environment without Node or Python and an identified release candidate.
scenarios.when: Install, launch offline mode, complete the collaboration scenario, upgrade and close the application.
then: The installed application runs its bundled workers.
Installation explains the WebView2 bootstrapper requirement.
Artifacts, source revision, lockfiles, notices and observed acceptance are retained.
No worker processes remain after shutdown.

Representative supported Windows 10 and Windows 11 x64 client builds install and upgrade the same installer bytes. Each observation retains the OS build, WebView2 version, exact installer digest and independent installation and upgrade results.
scenarios.evidence_boundary: Actual clean-machine and packaged-runtime evidence; a native compilation alone cannot satisfy this scenario.

scenarios.user_goal: Inspect explicit synthetic examples without configuring or receiving an external service.
scenarios.given: Unconfigured startup, local generated examples and no credentials.
scenarios.when: Open the chart workspace, choose Open offline sample or deliberately visit #demo, select an instrument and timeframe, and compare candles, close-price line and volume.
then: The bare unconfigured workspace identifies its source state. Application operations and provider or model work wait for explicit user intent.
Instrument, timeframe and chart style controls, volume and time axis, instrument list and data inspection are available in the chart workspace.
Displayed identity and provenance agree with the Rust-validated history.
Late responses cannot overwrite a later selection and leaving the preview clears its chart.

A new profile shows no data and issues zero operations. Returning to the same explicitly selected sample visibly restores Simulated. Leaving it clears the source preference, including on a subsequent bare startup.
The chart consumes every page of one frozen input before displaying it. Size failures require a smaller request; only temporary admission failures offer a retry.
failure_cases: A later page belongs to a changed snapshot
An unavailable remembered source or invalid preference
scenarios.evidence_boundary: Browser checks cover the shared chart and loopback transport. M1-031 and M1-012 retain the Ubuntu Tauri/WebKitGTK field check. M1-011 retains the physical Windows WebView2 observation at matching inputs. Each observation records the actual host and actions.

scenarios.user_goal: Chart data from a purchased or self-produced folder and reuse the same mapping for the next delivery.
scenarios.given: A user-selected directory with differently structured CSV series, duplicates and known expected prices and volumes.
scenarios.when: Preview rows, correct a field or unit, chart the accepted data, add a file and refresh twice.
then: The chart agrees with independently expected values and identifies contributing files and rows.
A repeated refresh preserves counts. A changed file format requests review and the accepted revision remains available.

Import overlapping files in reverse enumeration order and obtain byte-equivalent accepted output with attributable source locators. Review competing corrections, replaced files, missing files and a withdrawal before atomically publishing a new revision.

Compare raw and adjusted equities, a dated future and a separately identified continuous/approximate series. Inspect unresolved units, same-time rows, missing cumulative baselines and session mappings. The earlier frozen snapshot remains replayable or explicitly unavailable.
failure_cases: Unknown adjustment basis or night-session date
Conflicting values have no authoritative correction order
An adjustment factor, volume baseline, auction calendar or roll rule is unavailable
scenarios.evidence_boundary: Exercise the local product entry. Private owner files and external provider access have independent evidence.

scenarios.user_goal: Arrange a workspace manually or by asking the AI, then revisit the same arrangement.
scenarios.given: One main chart, a watchlist, an inspection panel and a known workspace revision.
scenarios.when: Move the watchlist, link the table, pin a comparison, preview and apply the edit, save a layout and reopen it.
then: The same settings drive direct, declarative and AI edits. Selecting an instrument updates the linked table while preserving the pinned selection.
The user can undo the change or restore the default. Source, AI activity and confirmation controls stay reachable.

Hover and temporary navigation preserve the committed selection token and unsaved layout. Explicitly selecting another row or document passage advances the selection token independently of the durable workspace revision. Returning from temporary evidence restores the original viewport and independent pinned panels.

The user can add or remove an inspection table and switch the chart and table between compatible authorized bar sources. Both views identify the selected source. Reopening the named layout restores its arrangement and checks each data binding against current access.
failure_cases: Invalid layout version or stale AI edit
A queued annotation targets yesterday’s selected row after explicit reselection
A saved widget binding points to an incompatible, disconnected or revoked source
scenarios.evidence_boundary: This scenario exercises the built-in chart layout and allowlisted interactions. The original chart-free workbench has its own V1 acceptance.

scenarios.user_goal: Decide which information is visible, when it belongs on screen, how it looks and what selecting it opens.
scenarios.given: A blank workbench, a selected synthetic research note and an authorized local set of disclosures with known issuers, publication times and evidence identifiers.
scenarios.when: Compose a view that pairs matching disclosures with the note. Change its structure with the embedded AI and then adjust one element manually. Refresh the source, inspect a match, undo, save and reopen. Preview a draft that cannot be rendered.
then: The user can remove all default regions, build a presentation without a dedicated product widget and change its content rule or visual arrangement without rebuilding the application.
Only entitled matching items appear after refresh. A healthy empty result is distinguishable from unavailable coverage. The selected original and the saved note retain their identities.
After a failed draft the trusted host restores the accepted workbench. A reopened composition retains its rules and rechecks current permissions.
failure_cases: Previously saved chart layout opened after upgrade
scenarios.evidence_boundary: Verify the interaction in the desktop application and on the exact packaged Windows candidate at release. A screenshot, a standalone renderer probe or a preset dashboard cannot establish this result.

scenarios.user_goal: Discuss evidence out loud, correct what the AI understood and continue from that object in text.
scenarios.given: A user-selected provider and model with verified voice capability, authorized microphone and data scope, and a chart with a known local disclosure fixture.
scenarios.when: Ask whether the disclosure explains a price move, compare the published passage and chart in one timezone, interrupt with a corrected instrument or interval, then continue in text.
then: The chart marks the observed move and publication time. The source view highlights the passage. The AI distinguishes the observed sequence from a causal inference.
The corrected selection and the confirmed tool outcome are visible. Stopping speech and cancelling work produce their respective states.

In authorized real text and duplex sessions bind fixture, provider, route, model and modality to redacted outcomes. Confirm an exact mixed-language instrument, date, decimal price, quantity and unit before a write. An ambiguous or corrected value requires clarification and a fresh evidence calculation.

After Stop microphone inspect capture/transmission state and pending work separately. An interrupted or denied request cannot produce an execution claim. Changing destination or charge basis waits for a fresh choice.
failure_cases: Access denied or original target unavailable
Selected model supports text but lacks realtime audio
A proposed fallback changes the charge or external destination
The recognized contract month, decimal point or time zone changes a material value
A pending model call completes after microphone capture stops
A connected provider accepts text but its tested voice modality is missing
scenarios.evidence_boundary: A mock or text-only run cannot verify real voice. Keep raw audio private and retain only authorized redacted test observations. The disclosure fixture does not verify a network information channel.

scenarios.user_goal: Decide whether a move changes my thesis and review my reasoning later.
scenarios.given: A synthetic instrument, two attributable revisions and the user's stated horizon and reason for considering a purchase.
scenarios.when: Ask whether to buy after a price rise. Challenge an explanation, correct a time window, request an annotation and choose whether to save the decision. Revisit it after later prices become available.
then: The AI surfaces contrary evidence, recomputes the comparison for the corrected interval, states the uncertainty and lets the user choose. It can ask about a conflict with the user's own rule. Deliberation alone changes no chart or account state.

The authorized annotation has a visible core receipt. A saved note retains the contemporaneous alternatives and disagreement. Review distinguishes a gain or loss from faulty reasoning or incorrect input. The user can remove the note.

Use a unique synthetic phrase. Declining to save leaves no body, transcript or derived summary on disk. Explicitly save, delete, restart and search live state, indexes, logs, diagnostics and new exports for the phrase. A known deletion survives restoring an older backup. Restoring an independent copy without the marker warns before it makes old text visible.
failure_cases: A data correction arrives after the decision
A favorable outcome follows an unsupported thesis
User declines to save or share the note
A restored attachment, a previously shared excerpt, another profile or a private summary appears in the next outbound request
User cancels a restore after the warning
A backup includes an older copy but a newer deletion marker exists
A new model requests a deleted note
scenarios.evidence_boundary: Local decision-note checks cover explicit retention, dated review, later outcomes, deletion and staged note-only backup recovery. Configured dialogue has its own verification. A simulated or realized return is not an acceptance metric.

scenarios.user_goal: Use my preferred AI application to inspect the exact chart on screen and visibly annotate it.
scenarios.given: A running workspace showing the opt-in synthetic sample and a user-enabled local MCP connection scoped to that workspace.
scenarios.when: From Codex CLI, read the selected chart, request an annotation, inspect the result in ScopeHub and undo it. Repeat independently from a compatible desktop AI client.
then: The read identifies the same instrument, interval, source and revision visible to the user. ScopeHub identifies the requesting client and exposes only selected data. Read-only access rejects the first annotation.
After a write grant the annotation appears once on the user's chart and can be undone. A changed revision, a different workspace or a revoked grant produces a visible denial with no new effect.

Pair two independent clients, grant one only time and close and leave volume unknown for a separately granted test. Verify absent unauthorized fields and null authorized-unknown fields in successful responses, activity, errors, replay and reconnect. Moving the pointer does not invalidate an authorized target; explicit selection of another row does.
failure_cases: Client requests a field outside its entitlement
Client disconnects after the core committed a mutation
The user changes selection before the write
User denies a required confirmation in ScopeHub
An external client or cloud connector requests fields licensed for display only
A revoked client attempts to replay another session’s receipt
scenarios.evidence_boundary: Automated bridge checks cover local transport, concurrency and authorization. A product claim for a named client also needs the observed real client version, host and protected output. A fixture or CLI trace alone cannot establish desktop compatibility.

scenarios.user_goal: Review a text route once and continue ordinary questions from the workspace.
scenarios.given: A disconnected profile and an owned synthetic HTTP endpoint implementing the selected chat surface.
scenarios.when: Ask without a route, review and enable a configured connection, complete two turns and cancel or disconnect it. Choose the offline mock separately.
then: The first question and route setup produce zero outbound requests.
Two scoped HTTP requests reach the disclosed endpoint. The second includes the prior successful pair and the actual responding model is visible.
Failure does not substitute a mock. After cancellation, disconnection or replacement, an old grant cannot dispatch. The mock sends no HTTP requests.
scenarios.evidence_boundary: The peer is a synthetic HTTP fixture. Model capability, finance collaboration and packaged Windows behavior have independent acceptance gates.

scenarios.user_goal: Keep chart data current as a local sync folder receives new deliveries.
scenarios.given: On Friday a profile has approved one directory and mapping. A chart follows its current revision; an earlier analysis holds a frozen revision.
scenarios.when: Close the desktop. Add a compatible file and alias, atomically replace a synced file with its old observations plus a new day, and change an old close in another series. Reopen on Monday; interrupt and retry a refresh.
then: Import complete compatible additions once. Display the historical conflict and keep the prior accepted value until reviewed. The earlier analysis rereads its original revision.
Show the saved scope and last success in settings. A paused, disconnected, replaced or revoked directory cannot publish new data.
failure_cases: Root replacement, symlink escape or different profile
Grant revoked between preview and commit
scenarios.evidence_boundary: Exercise an installed host where native identity is available and repeat the restart scenario with synthetic files. Historical manual CSV evidence covers the session picker.

scenarios.user_goal: Chart a locally owned daily series and inspect its two auction sessions without reformatting the files.
scenarios.given: Synthetic inputs use a bare six-character daily code, exchange-qualified auction codes, an ambiguous venue, a missing auction, and an absent adjustment factor.
scenarios.when: Preview the mapping, inspect source units and adjustment basis, publish and reread the resulting revisions.
then: A missing opening auction leaves the daily and closing observations visible. A raw value with unknown adjustment stays traceable.
Same-code instruments from different venues, daily and auction quantities, source rows and mapping versions stay distinguishable.
scenarios.evidence_boundary: Use synthetic records in hosted checks. The independent owner sample inspection establishes only its observed file characteristics.

scenarios.user_goal: Apply a named research method and inspect the evidence behind its conclusion.
scenarios.given: An equity chart is selected. One case supplies statements available on the analysis date and one supplies price data alone.
scenarios.when: Request an owner-earnings analysis, then change the maintenance capital estimate.
then: Identify the method version and sources, reproduce the arithmetic and surface assumptions and contrary evidence.
Describe the missing inputs in the chart-only case and recheck rights when the evidence changes.
scenarios.evidence_boundary: Replay fixes inputs and tool responses. Real-model behavior retains its separate qualification.

scenarios.user_goal: Use files the user downloaded and an API they obtained directly from its provider.
scenarios.given: A fresh profile has no ScopeHub account, first-party data plan or model. A controlled read-only provider accepts a synthetic test credential.
scenarios.when: Open Settings > Data sources > My data sources, select the user’s local directory, enter the supplied API connection details, test a bounded read and reopen the saved connection.
then: The local files, personally entered records and external API retain their independent provenance and rights. The external form displays the required inputs for its provider. Secrets stay in the selected connector’s credential store.
Complete setup and refresh on the fresh local profile. Removing one source leaves the others usable.
failure_cases: Multiple independent sources covering one instrument
scenarios.evidence_boundary: Use a controlled provider in product acceptance. Real feed rights, service subscriptions and billing are verified separately.

artifact_requirements: Committed source revision and execution-input digest

The report binds runs/<run-id>/candidate/build-manifest.json to its SHA-256. Within candidate/, retain the same hashed NSIS installer and separately hashed clean-install and upgrade observations on Windows 10 and Windows 11 x64 client builds.
product_review: Have the owner reshape a workbench from blank on the candidate and inspect its behavior after a source refresh and reopen.
Demonstrate the end-to-end workflow to the owner and record observed usability issues as feedback.
Compare the delivered outcome with the research question, visible source quality and actual operation results.
Use release-artifacts acceptance to verify retained artifacts and the recorded owner review; a checklist alone is not acceptance.

candidate: Reassess release readiness after integration of a planned user-visible outcome, a material defect fix or a packaging/dependency change affecting an existing release. A passing ordinary change run or elapsed calendar time alone is not a release trigger.

The current first product release targets the accepted M0-M5 contract and delivery scenarios. M0 alone is a scaffold checkpoint. A narrower preview or changed product release target needs an explicit scoped requirement and accurately labeled limitations; never silently remove unmet acceptance gates.

Create a bounded release task naming target version/channel, exact clean main commit, included scenarios, known issues, native acceptance and recovery plan. Confirm successful CI for that actual main revision before spending time on packaging.

Build the candidate once with pinned inputs; retain installer, bundled-worker manifest, hashes, notices and logs outside the temporary CI retention window. Run the Windows release profile and observe clean-machine installation, use, upgrade, recovery and stability against those exact bytes.

Have the owner exercise the intended workflow and retain actual feedback. A code-review approval, mock result or checklist does not replace product review. Changed source, build inputs or packaged bytes invalidate the affected candidate acceptance; create and verify a new candidate.
publication: Use project:readiness as a technical assessment, then present the concrete version/channel, source commit, artifact hashes, retained acceptance, owner product review, known limitations and recovery procedure. A passing result does not grant publication permission.

Publish only within explicit owner release authorization covering that candidate or an applicable previously granted scope. Authorization to merge does not authorize publication. Keep the release draft while evidence or authorization is pending.

Before publishing, recheck candidate identity and blockers; bind the version tag to the accepted main commit and publish the tested artifacts without rebuilding. Preserve existing published versions and tags; a correction gets a new version.

Verify the published tag/commit, downloadable asset hashes and installation smoke result, retain the release record and update the next task. The publisher and executable release-artifacts gate are implemented under packaging work before the first actual release, not claimed present by this policy.
recovery: A failed candidate remains unpublished. Retain the failing artifacts/logs, open corrective work, repair and repeat affected acceptance on the new candidate.

After an integration regression, retain the exact main commit and failing CI, then prepare a reviewed repair or revert PR through the same gates. Do not force-rewrite main or treat a previous branch run as validation of the merged revision.

After a released defect, record affected versions, stop further promotion, tell the owner the observed impact and prepare a fix or withdrawal within applicable authorization. Retain evidence and existing version identity; do not silently replace downloads.
For stateful upgrades, use the tested backup/restore or forward-repair procedure. Reverting application code does not prove that persisted user data can safely be downgraded.

checkpoint: Deliver one observable outcome per short-lived branch and pull request. Keep its contract, implementation, regression and related fixes together in reviewable commits. Start from reviewed current main and name the dependency and integration order for a stacked delivery.
Make a coherent local commit after a meaningful validated outcome, before a risky experiment, and at handoff. Inspect the diff and include only intended project files.

Use a task branch such as codex/<outcome>. For a recognized narrow change, run its selected checks locally. For a change requiring full CI, run the affected tests locally and use the protected jobs for the complete cross-platform suite. Complete the task's required checks with local or matching hosted evidence before marking it done. Retain unresolved failures explicitly in recovery checkpoints.
Use project:checkpoint to inspect the commit, dirty files, locally known upstream distance, current fast checks and slowest checks. It does not fetch or prove remote synchronization.
A local commit preserves recoverable source; an archived task receipt preserves observed acceptance. Keep both and distinguish them from push, integration and release.
push: Within owner-authorized publication scope, push meaningful checkpoints and handoffs to the task branch and create or update its draft pull request. Do not push every edit or wait for product completion.
The current workflow runs on pull requests and main pushes. A branch push without a pull request does not start it; keep pull requests open while iterating.
Record branch, commit and pull-request URL. A network error, missing upstream or queued run leaves synchronization or verification pending, not complete.
Run project:ci after pushing, creating a pull request or observing a CI completion. Continue independent work while it runs; recheck the current commit before using the result.
verification: Select verification from the complete difference between the reviewed base and the checked candidate for each pull request and main push. Run the selected profile in both protected jobs, with accepted-history validation and a fresh dependency review. The report records every omitted check. Use project:impact to preview the decision locally.

Use the full change suite for shared, sensitive, unknown or ambiguous changes, for the weekly main regression and for a manual full run. Run release-cadence checks on an identified release candidate or through an affected task when the change calls for them.

Require the latest matching workflow run for the exact source commit to succeed; missing, queued, cancelled, timed-out and failed runs are not passes. A successful workflow still does not complete unimplemented task or release gates.

Record both the pull-request head and the actual checked-out merge commit. Archive only evidence with matching execution inputs, task and decision definitions, origin, commit identity and unchanged log digests.

Download artifacts using the authenticated official gh CLI into .reports/ci/<run-id>/<platform>; pass that directory with project:record --artifact-root. Preserve the original report and never replace local latest reports with downloaded files.

CI metadata and hashes provide traceability and stale-evidence detection, not cryptographic attestation against a malicious contributor. Retrieve evidence from the observed repository run and review changes to the checks themselves.

Accepted completed tasks may append supplementary validated receipts while preserving every non-evidence field and the original ordered evidence references. Added receipts must match that accepted task definition and pass all its checks. Cancelled tasks and accepted ADRs remain immutable. Compare both the PR base and the previous pushed checkpoint when available.

Supply a verified Windows release report with project:readiness --candidate <main-sha> --report .reports/ci/<run-id>/windows/test-report.json --artifact-root .reports/ci/<run-id>/windows. The report binds the candidate manifest, installer, client OS observations and logs. Keep the local latest report intact.

Before integration, bind both successful harness steps to the required scope, pull request number, head and base revisions. Examine newer task-specific failures for the delivered behavior and retain a regression for a reproduced defect.
integration: Integrate through a reviewed pull request with successful required checks for its current revision. Recheck after base changes, conflicts or consequential new evidence.

Require Linux and Windows verification before normal integration. Keep branch protection settings aligned with actual job names once their first successful runs are observed; repository policy text alone does not enforce GitHub settings.
Keep source integration, packaging and public release separate. A merged pull request is not a released or product-accepted build.

Retain release artifacts, checksums and acceptance evidence outside ephemeral CI retention when releases are implemented. The current workflow retains diagnostic artifacts for 30 days; task receipts keep digests, not full logs.

Run pnpm project:protection before integration and after workflow job-name or repository-setting changes. It compares live main protection with project/branch-protection.json using the owner-pinned official gh account; missing access and drift fail. This local owner check is deliberately outside unprivileged build CI and does not grant merge permission.

The integration unit is a coherent completed task or a tightly related group with archived acceptance, a reviewable diff and a recovery direction. Split unfinished behavior into a later task/PR or keep it unreachable; future planned milestones alone do not block integration. Open a fresh task branch from current main after integration.

Run project:integration --pr <number> after task closure, after CI completion when a delivery is complete, at handoff, and immediately before an authorized merge. It reads live PR head/base, latest workflow jobs, server protection, current local source, completed scope and relevant feedback; unavailable or changing observations remain blocked. A draft can be ready to present for review while still ineligible to merge.

Present a merge proposal naming the PR, head/base revisions, delivered tasks, verification, material limits and recovery plan. Review the actual diff and unresolved conversations. Owner review may be recorded in the conversation for this single-owner repository; an empty GitHub reviewDecision or zero required external approvals never proves that review occurred.

Keep technical assessment, observed review and operation authorization separate. Reuse already granted applicable merge scope; otherwise obtain explicit merge authorization for the concrete proposal. A new head/base requires renewed assessment and review of its delta. Do not infer merge or release permission from repair, push, draft-PR or CI authorization.

For an authorized merge, check the PR head again and use an expected-head guard such as gh pr merge --match-head-commit <sha>; preserve strict server checks and never use an admin bypass. Record the actual main merge commit and inspect its push workflow. A merged PR with failed main CI is an integration incident, not release-ready source.

After verifying the main push, confirm retirement of the integrated head. Before merging a branch that another open pull request uses as its base, integrate or retarget the dependent work and reverify it. If another integration already contains a whole pull request head, verify its exact ancestry and record the containing main change before closing that pull request.
failure_recovery: Keep the failed run and inspect its first actionable error. Record consequential escapes or false assumptions as feedback with a corrective task and regression evidence.
Reproduce with the smallest relevant local or native check; fix on the branch, commit and rerun the affected checks plus required integration gates.
Retry a transient infrastructure failure only after recording its cause. Do not retry assertions repeatedly, loosen checks, use stale green runs or hide cancellation to obtain a passing status.
If a regression reaches main, create a repair or revert commit and reverify. Preserve shared history; do not force-push to erase the failure.

Before retiring a ref outside main history, review all unique changes, recover original acceptance evidence, and verify restoration of its exact tip from independent storage. Check fresh protected refs and every open pull request head and base before deletion. Bind each deletion to the observed SHA with a per-ref lease. Restore a missing name from the verified bundle with an empty expected-value lease. Local worktree cleanup also requires its separate evidence and activity checks.
scaling: Use a five-minute fast-feedback objective and a fifteen-minute change-CI objective to trigger investigation. The change job timeout is 30 minutes on Linux and 60 minutes on Windows. The release job timeout is 180 minutes. Keep required checks in place while reviewing slow runs.

Use recorded check durations and job queue time to find the bottleneck. Cache pnpm, uv and Cargo dependencies and build outputs by platform, toolchain and lockfiles; caches never count as test evidence.

Use project:checkpoint for the current checkout and project:timing for retained timing observations. Use project:timing --run <id> or --recent for explicit Actions inspection with pinned official gh and fetch only compact timing artifacts. Save observations under .reports/timing or in the development archive for offline review. Queue spans run creation to job start on the first attempt. Setup, harness step and tail partition the completed job when timestamps are present. Workflow elapsed ends at the last verification job; runner work sums job spans. Summed check durations can overlap and never substitute for elapsed time.

For a new or materially slower required check, record representative before and after elapsed time and runner work, assign the existing implementation or corrective task, and choose scope and cadence against the accepted risk. Preserve required coverage or review its replacement with equivalent evidence. Use normal runs and targeted measurements without duplicating full CI for routine changes.

Use the generated-contracts comparison in project:timing to observe repeated PR and main work when both successful jobs have matching merge inputs, scope, platform, command and tools. Missing observations stay unknown. Both jobs execute and supply their own results.

When repeated runs exceed the objective, split independent checks into jobs, isolate long stability work, and add measured task-specific selection. Preserve a required aggregate result and explicit coverage of omitted checks.
Keep generated-contract, architecture, task-state and relevant regressions early. Add scheduled validation or paid/self-hosted runners only when an observed need justifies the recurring resource use.

triggers: A check, build, task command or evidence import fails, including failure before a harness report exists.
Observed product or scaffold behavior contradicts an accepted requirement even when all existing checks pass.
The current concrete task needs a missing check, adapter, fixture, boundary or recovery capability; future planned checks alone are not maintenance incidents.
The same workaround or failure recurs, or measured feedback times repeatedly exceed source_control.scaling objectives.
workflow: During authorized development the active development AI owns diagnosis, repair, regression evidence and resumption for both scaffold and product defects. CI reports failures. Repair runs in an active development session and resumes from the ledger and retained evidence. Check for problems at task start, on failures and before completion. At startup and handoff, inspect the retained failure signals in project:status and the integration and weekly observations in project:ci. If a retained-run scan is incomplete, inspect the reported unavailable originals and any older run directories starting with first_omitted_run_id. Match serious untriaged failures to their corrective feedback before reporting a clean handoff. Keep missing originals visible when recovery cannot establish the outcome. A missing weekly observation or one more than eight days old needs review. The interval allows one day beyond the weekly schedule. The active development AI follows up without an owner reminder. Keep the original run and platform when classifying an environment issue or opening corrective work. Continue independent work while waiting for field evidence.

Retain the failed run, original control files and interrupted task id using project:recover --task <id> --save. The diagnostic is read-only apart from its isolated snapshot and does not validate acceptance.

Reproduce the smallest failing behavior and classify the cause as product defect, scaffold defect, environment issue, incorrect expectation or concrete capability gap. A missing executable is not evidence that source code is wrong; a passing suite is not evidence against an observed defect.

Keep a routine repair within the active task. For consequential new scope, create a corrective task with a plan, record feedback, preserve the interrupted task and next action, and switch focus. Do not rewrite completed task definitions or accepted decisions.

Use a failing regression, contract vector, minimal fixture or bounded experiment to capture the intended behavior before fixing it. For each material failure in the active plan, use the earliest entry point that can distinguish valid from invalid input. Exercise the rejection before a write, external call or acceptance decision when the information is available there. Verify that the last accepted state survives. For evidence that only a native or external interaction can supply, reject missing evidence on admission and keep the dependent claim blocked. Reuse, extend, replace or remove a component according to the concrete need and lifetime cost; register new implemented checks and their scenario or change-type bindings.

Make the smallest demonstrable repair and run the regression through the affected entry point. Use the broader checks appropriate to its scope and revise the hypothesis when evidence contradicts it. Two failures with the same evidence trigger a smaller reproduction or comparison with a reviewed checkpoint.

Restore normal project validation and required integration checks, archive matching task evidence, close consequential feedback with cause/correction/prevention, then restore focus and resume the interrupted task when unblocked. Preserve unresolved blockers and continue independent work. At intake, each regression check needs a linked task that owns it. When a linked task becomes active, include the assigned serious regressions in its risk plan and exercise the first normal entry that should reject each invalid case. Register the observation before running its regression. The local project check and harness compare feedback with HEAD and the unique common ancestor of the locally tracked protected branch before executing checks. Explicit local review and checkpoint revisions allow the protected job to compare both histories. Preserve accepted incoming records at their original scope when they match the independently reviewed base. For a new major or critical resolution, protected history verifies that the linked receipts cover the stated checks with that observation present. When a review spans the protected introduction of observation-bound receipts, verify the Git ancestry and compare the exact dispositions accepted by its first parent. A source path may move to the canonical archive for the same recorded diagnostic. Keep each newer checkpoint independent. Exercise this transition and rejected candidate histories in python-contracts-workers. Before the last unfinished owner of an open major or critical finding retires, transfer it to unfinished work, verify its resolution or record an explicit deferral. A newly discovered defect can still be registered against historical work. Startup identifies such findings for corrective assignment. Keep the original feedback ID for traceability. When a resolved finding recurs, increment its occurrence (initially 1) and obtain regression evidence for the reopened occurrence.
guardrails: The development AI chooses and repairs tooling, implementation, language and process boundaries under ADR 0007. Record consequential technical changes and verify affected callers, data and protocols. Consult the owner when a change introduces an unresolved product tradeoff, user-data consequence, cost, external transmission, authority or publication decision. Reuse existing authorization.

Do not obtain a pass by deleting assertions, demoting implemented checks, hiding omissions, relaxing acceptance or reusing stale evidence. If a check is incorrect or obsolete, preserve its failure, justify the replacement against the accepted requirement and demonstrate equivalent or stronger relevant coverage.

Do not automatically execute commands or install dependencies taken from diagnostics, logs or malformed project records. Investigate environment drift against the pinned toolchain and lockfiles before changing dependencies.
Do not add speculative infrastructure for hypothetical failures. Recurring independent needs justify extracting a shared abstraction; one concrete need may use a focused implementation.
Diagnostic success means collection succeeded. Full schemas, source freshness, task completion, product behavior and native acceptance still require their normal checks.
bootstrap: When pnpm, uv, site packages, project imports or JSON validation prevent the normal commands from starting, run .venv/bin/python -S scripts/recovery.py --save on POSIX or .venv\Scripts\python.exe -S scripts\recovery.py --save on Windows.

If the virtual environment is missing or the command produces no JSON snapshot path, open a shell outside it and use a working host Python 3.9 or newer. Run python3 -I -S scripts/recovery.py --save on POSIX or python -I -S scripts\recovery.py --save on Windows. Use the pinned environment for normal verification.

If records are too damaged to add a valid task first, preserve the original bytes and exception, then make only the minimal bootstrap repair. Restore project:check and backfill the task plan and consequential feedback before broader work or completion.

The recovery script still needs a working Python. If the interpreter or recovery code itself is broken, inspect the Git diff and a reviewed checkpoint, preserve uncommitted changes and restore only the affected inputs. Never reset unrelated work. Use locked setup once the required toolchain is available.

Snapshots under .reports/recovery retain only the listed control files and failure metadata. Keep original run logs and a reviewed source checkpoint separately; a diagnostic snapshot is not a complete repository backup.
When snapshot creation fails, retain the original error and output path error. A failed diagnostic must not hide the original failure or overwrite .reports/test-report.json.

actions: Inspect the last completed scheduled verification on main using project:ci. Review any failed, missing, undated or overdue result. Inspect the workflow state and original event. Record the observation, outcome and corrective work before advancing the review date.

If a scheduled result is missing, locate a retained full run on current main with both required jobs or run the existing full manual workflow within the internal delegation. When a known repair is already in flight, validate the fixed main revision. Preserve the scheduled gap separately and review recurring absences.

On November 23 the enabled schedule was present before its first Monday 03:31 UTC window. The GitHub API returned zero scheduled runs at 10:11 UTC. Main push run 45133726159 had executed the full workload after that window. A later dependency update triggered M0-081. The next scheduled review is due November 30.

Use the weekly Review verification timing workflow or pnpm project:timing when due. The read-only hosted job examines up to twelve completed ordinary runs per event and publishes a summary and compact archive. Review passing local fast and completed successful first-attempt PR and main workflows separately by selected profile, platform, runner, Cargo cache observation and exact selected check outcomes. Warm means exact archive restoration, partial means a matched prefix restored, not_restored means an attempted restore reported no matched archive, not_requested means the reviewed task skipped restoration, and unknown means unavailable observations. A missing match can also follow a service or extraction error. Reserve cold for an independently observed empty build target. Build reuse depends on the restored contents and current inputs.

Investigate two objective breaches among the latest three comparable runs, or a median increase of at least 60 seconds and 15 percent between consecutive sets of three comparable runs, even under budget. Compare individual stages and slow checks, record the source and coverage, and assign a corrective task for persistent regressions. Investigate a single outlier and collect more observations without a timing gate. Record missing or changed coverage and start a comparable baseline before making a speed claim.

For comparable product slices, compare median time from work start to the first observed usable interaction and from PR creation to verified main. Record missing observations explicitly. Review first-attempt failures, retries and defects found after merge alongside elapsed time before changing coverage or cadence.

Apply the elapsed objective across coverage changes within the same feedback scope. Review added and removed checks and compare the latest median to a stable faster three-run window when recent scope expansion follows an improvement. Record missing compact history, keep incomplete and release or task runs available as diagnostics, and advance the review date after recording findings and follow-up.

The 2026-11-21 baseline review found repeated Windows overruns and substantial setup and harness costs across three retained PR and main pairs. M0-046 owns the first repair and its comparable follow-up. Continue retaining the paired platform observations and review again by 2026-11-28.

Run pnpm project:branches at the next active session when due and after an integration. Fetch missing history from the reviewed origin and repeat the observation. Run pnpm project:protection to compare effective main settings against policy and confirm automatic head deletion in the branch inventory.

Trace each retained remote head to its active task, dependent pull request, or independent recovery copy. Resolve an integrated head, failing dependency proposal or abandoned stack and record the result.
Run pnpm project:worktree retirement with the development archive root and pnpm project:storage. Inspect active processes, private refs, dirty files and original evidence on held checkouts.
Retire a clean idle checkout after its source and evidence have a verified recovery path. Record the disposition of unique work. Regenerate the observation immediately before each removal.

Before releasing a temporary review directory, find feedback records that use its outputs. Copy original observations to a durable location, verify their file digests and record the logical source and manifest digest.

Keep task-owned staging that outlives its creating process under the task report directory when feasible. For an external clone, build target or review fixture, record its owner, location and retirement condition in the private task handoff.

Review known project-owned staging outside registered worktrees, including temporary roots used by completed tasks. Check live processes, linked checkouts and evidence references. Retain needed originals in a verified archive with a restoration index, then release the identified idle paths and record the outcome.

For a compatibility path touched since the previous review, identify the supported consumer, contract version, data migration or original evidence reader and exercise the relevant regression. Track temporary aliases or bridges with a removal condition and responsible task.

Remove a duplicate or expired path after confirming its callers, retained data and rollback story. Keep the shared implementation and an independent expected behavior test. Review dependencies on the separate schedule in project/dependencies.json.
